deliverable: A source-grounded summary of what two Bilibili course-opening videos announce about a data-structures course and an exam-prep video series, with per-segment locators, ASR caveats, and no slide-level claims.

turns.text: Using only these two captured openings, summarize what each lecturer announces about the subject, the course plan, the teaching materials, and the study method. Separate video A from video B and give the ASR segment locator for each point.

Video A only: how does the speaker justify the course's importance, what sequence of material does he announce from the introductory chapter onward, and what does he say about how other courses use the subject? Do not add material he does not say.

Video B only: what does the speaker say about the textbook, about how students should use the videos, and for which exam audiences the series is intended? Keep to the opening minutes and mark anything the ASR garbles instead of guessing it.

acceptable_partial_outcomes: The transcripts cover only the opening minutes of each video; answers must not claim slide, frame, caption or other on-screen content, nor any part of either video beyond the captured opening.
The ASR is noisy and mixes Simplified and Traditional characters; a garbled personal name, chapter label, course list, or exercise reference must be reported as unclear rather than repaired.
The course map in video A cannot be reconstructed in full from the captured speech, and the exam-planning details in video B are only partly captured.

reference_review.method: quotes sliced from ASR snapshots and re-checked as literal substrings

authority_anchors.supports: The MIT 6.006 course description lists 'common algorithms, algorithmic paradigms, and data structures' as one subject and says the course 'emphasizes the relationship between algorithms and programming'; independent confirmation that data structures and algorithms are taught as a joint foundation of programming, the pairing the speaker states as program = data structures + algorithms. It is not evidence for the speaker's own sentences.
